subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chats automatically provision per-sender subagents with isolated skills/config/memory, or should OpenClaw keep sender-scoped group sessions as the supported isolation model and track subagent/skill policy separately?
rationale: The current source has partial session and subagent infrastructure, but the requested behavior changes channel routing, agent lifecycle, memory isolation, skills, config writes, and security boundaries, which requires maintainer product/security intent.

options.title: Keep as Feishu product design
options.body: Use this issue as the umbrella decision for whether Feishu should get automatic group sender subagents, then split approved implementation into narrow API/plugin/migration tasks.

options.title: Narrow to session scopes
options.body: Treat group_sender and group_topic_sender as the supported current isolation model and close or rewrite the automatic subagent parts as out of scope.

options.title: Defer to related API issues
options.body: Route account identity, channel subagent threading, and skill preferences to their related open issues before revisiting automatic Feishu group subagents.

recommendation.title: Keep as Feishu product design
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the umbrella decision for whether Feishu should get automatic group sender subagents, then split approved implementation into narrow API/plugin/migration tasks.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest current-code owner for the Feishu session, dynamic-agent, and subagent-hook paths involved in the decision.
